utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Call the case, please, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are starting 10 minutes late because the previous Chamber surpassed their time limit by 10 minutes. So once again, I should like to tell all the parties that we must respect the hearing sittings, the time for them, and we'll have to end by 7.00 p.m. That's the first point. Secondly, I'd like to say good afternoon to everybody in the courtroom, including the witness, and I'm going to give the floor to the registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. We have one IC document for today. That is the 6D reply to the Prosecution response to the Defence exhibits tendered through Witness Josip Praljak. This document will be assigned Exhibit number IC 474. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now, as far as time is concerned, I'm going to give the floor to Mr. Ibrisimovic. He'll have 60 minutes. And if he does not use up all his time, it can be used by Mr. Prlic, who will have 60 minutes plus any time left over from Mr. Ibrisimovic. Then the Stojic Defence will have 75 minutes, and 10 minutes for redirect from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We do have a few questions for this witness in order to clarify something that he has testified about over the past two days.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Biskic.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to refer to you as Mr. Biskic so as to avoid general, brigadier, or whatever other titles may have been used. I would first of all like to ask you -- or, rather, I wouldn't like to ask you anything you've talked about, why you've come, how you came to be here, what your tasks were and what you did in respect of those tasks and assignments. My first question is this: It is about the work of Mr. Pusic or, rather, the office for exchange headed by Mr. Pusic. I think your knowledge about what Mr. Pusic did before you arrived in Bosnia-Herzegovina is not such that you can actually talk to us about it, that your knowledge in that area is limited; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: A little louder, please.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Your first contacts with Mr. Pusic and the work of his office was in fact when the implementation of the decision by Mr. Boban to disband the collection centres started; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: You said that that was in December, that that's when you received the first information about the collection centres. Now, I'm interested in whether you received that information before this decision or with respect to the implementation of the decision to disband the collection centres.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already answered that question. I've answered it over the past two days. It was in the first half of November 1993 that I became acquainted with the problem of the collection centres, and during the month of November I initiated a number of activities linked to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In that respect you issued some orders to your subordinates or, rather, proposals and guidelines to your subordinates [as interpreted] as to how to resolve the problems of these centres, and this refers to the order of the 17th of November, 1993, to Mr. Lavric to inform you what the situation was like and what was happening in the detainee centres; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like now to go back to the meeting --

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And, Mr. President, could the witness be shown a set of documents. I think that he'll be able to follow the proceedings more easily. I think the Trial Chamber has already received copies of those documents, full sets. Thank you. On page 3 of the transcript, line 13, it should say superiors and not subordinates.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Would you take a look at the document, P 07148. It is the minutes of the 11th of December, 1993. You've already looked at it. It's the second document in order, I think. The meeting lasted for more than two hours, so these are excerpts from the minutes, because it's not a stenographic rendition of everything that was stated at the meeting, and I think that's what you said too, did you not?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Among other things at this meeting, in addition to all the individuals listed here, Mr. Pusic also attended as head of the office for the exchange of prisoners of war; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Would you now take a look at page 5 of the original source document, and take it look at what it says at the end. It says after that the representatives of the organs mentioned determined -- or, rather, appointed the following people to realise the tasks. Then we have the Gabela centre, detainee centre. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, but what page are you referring to? Are we talking about -- I have the minutes of the 11th -- or, rather, the 13th of November. You said it was the first document, so that's the document I opened first.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: The number of the document is P 07148.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's fine. I have it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: So if you look at page 5, for Gabela, the people appointed to realise the decisions and tasks are listed, and we have a list of persons who should head the activities to disband these centres. If you look at this a bit more closely, Mr. Pusic was not appointed to any of these commissions -- or either of these commissions in charge of disbanding the detainee centres. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are right. These are teams who were supposed to divide up the detainees into the categories that we discussed previously.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: On page 6 we have listed the tasks to be implemented by the teams. Of that's precisely what you were saying; right?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: A list of the prisoners of war, the detainees, their classification, as you said.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, into four categories.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Now, these commissions, the ones that were established according to these minutes, did they inform you of their work?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at the very next meeting, the 13th, they submitted a report.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Can we now take a look at the minutes of the 13th. It is P 7143. That's the number of the document. And Mr. Pusic attended that meeting as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Ibrisimovic. You could greatly assist the Chamber by indicating the page in the English version also.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this document I wasn't referring to any particular page. I just asked the witness to take a look at the document, but I will, of course, follow your guidelines and state the page, and I apologise for not having done so previously.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Now, do you remember this meeting of the 13th of December, 1993?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: We've already spoken about that, and these commissions informed -- informed all those present at the meeting how far they had gone implementing the tasks assigned and among others they informed you too?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: I wanted to ask you, Mr. Pusic says here that the International Red Cross should be informed and be invited to attend the meeting to hear all this information and the report tabled. Do you remember at that?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is that on any page in this document? Does it say so? Well, anyway, in the implementation of this decision, from the very beginning the representatives of the Red Cross were included as were the representatives of the International Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: They played an active part, did they? And that's on page 3 of the original version, and I'll find the page in the English version for the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Judge Trechsel. Page 5 anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pusic suggests that Red Cross should be invited from Medjugorje.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that on the 11th of December it was stated that the representative of the Red Cross was -- did not come to the meeting although they had been invited, although I wasn't the one who invited him.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: So from the very beginning of the implementation of this decision the Red Cross was actively involved, i.e., they were invited to get involved in dealing with these problems?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you about the office of Mr. Pusic. He also played a role -- role in all this, given his office, he was the head of the office for exchange, and he had some information that might have been important for the implementation of the decision. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: When I listened to your testimony, you said that the office provided collective reports about all that.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at document P 7187. This is a report that my learned friend has already shown to you.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Here it says that Mr. Pusic, when he sent this report, he spoke in this report about the things that had already taken place a day before or two days before that?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: He doesn't say anything about what should be done in the future. He just provides a report about the activities that had been taken in the previous period.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Berislav Pusic reports on what was done between the 13th and the 15th of December and the report is dated the 15th of December.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: My learned friend showed you these documents. All these reports are very similar, and just for the record I'm going to say that these are documents number P 7246. This is another collective report about what had taken place with regard to the implementation of the decision. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a report dated 18 December. We already saw yesterday or the day before in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: When you look at these records and when we take into account what you have testified about, then the role of this office run by Mr. Pusic may be regarded as an office that assisted with dealing with all these problems by using the database that the office had at its disposal?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the description of the work of this service goes, I'm not familiar with it. I assume that they did have some records on the persons that were supposed to be exchanged, and obviously this report confirms that based on the data that they had and based on the reports of the teams. This is a collective report about the total number of detainees and where they were sent to eventually.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: You know that this also existed in the Croatian army, in the army of BiH, the army of Republika Srpska, that they had the same services or -- and they performed the same tasks. This was necessary under the conditions.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These services existed, but they were not part of the armed forces, however. They were just services of the Republic of Croatia. At least in the Republic of Croatia they were not part of the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Can you now look at document number P 7403. It is in the same binder.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: This is a request that Mr. Pusic sent to you personally; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: And he asks you to deliver lists that would help the regular work of the service; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at the following document. This is P 07488.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: The handwritten part, I don't know whether this is your handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: And it says that a copy was sent to Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a hand -- the handwriting of somebody from the police administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: And the police administration sent to Mr. Pusic --

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: -- and to you as well, lists of war detainees, prisoners of war. This was sent on the 6th of January?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: And on the following page is the list of the prisoners of war which had already been categorised.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the 6th of January, 1994, which means that this is a list of those who at the moment had remained in Heliodrom after the collection centres had been disbanded.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at the following document in the binder, the number is P 07494. This is a document that has already been shown to you by the Prosecutor, and you have already spoken about this document.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: This is a proposal by Mr. Pusic, at least this is what it says here. "We propose that the Heliodrom centre should be relieved of the burden and some of the detainees should be transferred to Gabela."

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: And you said that you are not in agreement?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: And that this is sent to whoever it should be sent to. I would like to ask you this: Mr. Pusic, obviously, if this is on the 6th of January, 1994, and would you say at that moment Gabela was not a military investigative prison. He didn't know it at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me put it this way. I said this: After the implementation of the decision on the disbanding of the collective centres we have defined that there was only the Heliodrom as the prisoners' centre and also the military prison in Ljubuski. As for other prisons or collection centres, I did not know at the time, neither did my superior, Mr. Jukic, tell me anything about them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: According to this Mr. Pusic did not have that information either, did he?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Say here I do not agree.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: So you don't agree that these people should be transferred from the Heliodrom to the Gabela centre?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I should explain. The security company was established to guard the Heliodrom, and during the implementation of the decision of the president of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna it was decided that all the detainees should remain in the Heliodrom price and those who should be transferred to prison they should be taken to prison. In agreement with that I did not accept this proposal, although I believe, and I said it already before that Mr. Berislav Pusic's proposal was well-meant because he wanted to improve the conditions at the Heliodrom by reducing the number of detainees there. I've already told you that I myself believe that their number was excessive and that it surpassed the capacity of the facility. And I will -- will also repeat what I said to him that the exchanges are on the way and that very soon the number of detainees will reduce in the Heliodrom; that's why I was not in agreement, and also because of the security issues because it's much -- much more difficult to provide security into different places simultaneously.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: What I'm trying to say is that Mr. Pusic could only issue a proposal. He could not issue an order to you.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He could not issue an order to me or to anybody else, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Let's look at another document which is P 08070. This is the last document in the binder. P 08070. You've already seen this document. My learned friend showed it to you.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: This is information, and we have also seen a couple of letters that the International Red Cross sent either to you or to somebody else, and also copied Mr. Pusic with all these letters.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to -- I would like to show you the last page of this document. This report was sent by Mr. Pusic to the International Red Cross, to UNPROFOR, to the monitors, amongst others.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I'd like to ask you this: When you had your interview, my learned friend Kruger asked you, and I believe this was about the meeting that took place on the 11th -- 11 December, 1993, you were the first to take the floor and you were followed by Mr. Pusic, and then Mr. Kruger said -- actually, he asked you if Mr. Pusic, who was the key person according to him a very important in all of that, and you said that he was not a very important person.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what I said, but I don't think I said that he wasn't important. Every person is important. However, at this meeting, depending on the way you look at it, we were all key persons or none of them -- none of us were.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions for this witness, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Ibrisimovic. Mr. Registrar, could you please tell me how much time did Mr. Ibrisimovic utilise for his cross. You may start.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This is rather too large for me. I'm short. I have a few issues to just clarify, and I'll start with: When you arrived in Bosnia-Herzegovina along with General Roso, it appears that the situation was rather confusing at times and a little chaotic, and therefore, based on at least from what I was able to understand your testimony, certain measures needed to be taken rather quickly. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I want to share to you a document, 1D 01246. This is a document signed by General Roso. It's dated -- it's dated 13 November 1993. And this is more for the benefit of the Trial Chamber. On page 1 we see this is a warning to all units and members of the Croatian Defence Council. And if you see where -- the underlined portion of that paragraph, we note that General Roso is being rather explicit that anyone who commits any crimes will be executed by firing squad. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And again this is just for the benefit of the Trial Chamber to show that at the time that you arrived and General Roso arrived the situation was such that -- at least the general thought that a certain warning needed to be issued. Now, let me move on to the next topic, and this deals with the ICRC. It's very clear from your testimony that you received letters from the ICRC, and upon receiving those letters you took certain measures. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I just want to point out again for the Chamber's benefit some things that would at least put things into perspective. First, if we could see 1D 01253. 1D 01253. This is a letter that's dated 12 -- 21/12/1993. Okay. You may not have this, sir. It may not be in B/C/S or in Croatian. It is in English, and I'll read the -- this is a letter to you where it begins, "Dear sir, we do thank you for your letter mentioning your appreciation towards the ICRC activities in favour of detainees." And then it goes on to say: "Allow us, sir, also to thank you for your personal involvement in the success of this operation to solve security problems. We are all determined at the ICRC to continue our humanitarian tasks in favour of all victims of the conflict." And this was also copied to Dr. Jadranko Prlic. But anyway, I want to share this with the Trial Chamber. Here is a recognition from the ICRC that you, sir, upon your arrival, at least, have begun close cooperation with the ICRC, and that would be correct, would it not, sir?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember, but probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, you indicated at some point --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas, I apologise for interrupting you, but isn't there some confusion here? You said that the letter was -- that a copy of the letter was sent to Mr. Prlic. I have the impression that this letter was sent to Mr. Prlic in person, personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm a little bit under the weather, Your Honour, and you're absolutely right. I apologise for that. Sorry. Let me -- and thank you for correcting me. It goes to show you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: And also, Mr. Karnavas, the witness does not seem to know this letter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. Right. I understand. I'm going to move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: So it's questionable whether it's admissible. In this context.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. I don't want to get into an evidence question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, at some point you indicated you were absent because you had a personal -- for personal reasons you had to go back to Croatia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from the 28th of January to the 25th of February, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But nonetheless, even though that you were absent, you had put measures in place for the continuation of the work that you had started, especially with respect to the ICRC; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And here by example again this -- this is Prosecution document 7796. I don't believe the Prosecution introduced this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To assist you again, you know that the Chamber likes to be of assistance to both parties, this letter from the Red Cross is in fact a reply to a letter sent to them by Mr. Prlic, and as far as the Defence is concerned, it would be a good idea, if that is possible, for you to give us, if you have it, a copy of the letter that Mr. Prlic sent to the Red Cross in his own interest.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So I take it now we're back to the previous document. Are we back to the previous document, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. I'll do this at some other point in time. The error was pointed out to me. Thank you again for clarifying that issue. Now I've moved on to another document, another set of questions, and the question was: When the gentleman was -- was absent, he had put measures in place with respect to the ICRC, and therefore now we are at 7798, 7798. This is a -- dated 3 February 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And this goes -- it says, "Subject: Report on the situation in Heliodrom." There is a report. And if we look at the last page, I believe, we see that somebody has signed it on your of what, I believe. Is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's a document that we were looking at yesterday and discussing, and this document was sent to the minister and General Roso from my office.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I confirm that all the documents coming in from the International Red Cross were complied with, whether I was down there myself or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Exactly. And that's the point I wanted to make, sir, to make sure that there was proof of that. Now, if we could go on to another document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, could you just be so kind as to show us where the date figures on the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Where are the date figures. Well, on the very first page it says, "Mostar 3 February 1994," at the very top where it says "Security sector." That's what mine says at least.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I don't doubt that. Ours does not. Maybe the cover -- the first page was missing, but you could still -- ours has a page report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, there should be a cover page along with that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: There should.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I cannot explain why it don't, but I'll make sure you'll have it at the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Moving right along. Now, if we could go on to 1D 01248, and this is -- we may have looked at it. This is an order, sir, by you, and is dated 29 March 1994. Do you see it, sir?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, do you have that document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And it's in reference to a letter dated 16th of March, but hear we see, sir, that you have -- explicitly in your order you have requested that certain things be done in reference to a letter that was provided to you and -- is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is an order which I mentioned, and I explained about it earlier on to the Prosecution, but it wasn't shown in the last few days, and it was -- refers to investigations of all abuse and mistreatment of war detainees, and I issued this order to the head of the military police and SIS and the Ministry of Defence and the chief of the Main Staff to his attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now -- thank you, sir. And the reason I mentioned this is because if we look at Prosecution document 8079, this is the letter that was actually sent by the ICRC. It's copied, among others, to Dr. Prlic. I don't know if you have it there, sir, but for the benefit of the Trial Chamber, I think if we -- if we take a look at Prosecution 8079 and we look at your order, they dovetail. I don't know if you have it, sir, there, but in any event, do -- and I take it the Trial Chamber is satisfied with that. Thank you. We can move on. Now, there is also, I want to point out, another document, and that is 1D 01254, because during your testimony questions have been raised with respect to numerous requests from the ICRC, and here we have -- this is dated 1 April 1994. Again, the document is 1254, and it's signed by Colonel Siljeg. And again this is for the court's benefit, if we go through the document, you can see in the various paragraphs which makes references to the various letters received, and the answers based on the investigations that were conducted. Does that not reflect that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I mentioned that report yesterday in response to a number of questions linked to letters from the ICRC. And this is a report by the head of the military police administration, and it speaks of what action was taken to 14 communications by the ICRC in a period of time --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, thank you --

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- ranging from January onwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. And, sir, again that was for the benefit because there were some questions as to whether any action was taken, and here we see that yes, indeed, when you were absent and while you were there responses to any requests by the international community were promptly dealt with. Now I'm going to move on to another topic, a topic that was not brought up by the -- by the Prosecution, though it was -- you were questioned about it very briefly. I mention this because I'm going outside the scope of the -- of the direct examination, but I don't intend to lead the witness. I have no need to. But, sir, after you left Bosnia-Herzegovina, you came back again, as I understand it, late June, early July; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in fact, the reason you came back was to assist, to assist, in an operation called Spider; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're quite right, an operation called Spider on the territory of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in fact, during that six-day interview, I notice there's one page -- a page and a half was devoted to that operation, but that operation essentially was an effort by the government to crack down on criminal activity and to investigate criminals, not just for regular crimes but also crimes against humanity or war crimes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That operation was planned and implemented in order to prevent all forms of disruption of law and order and crime on the territory of the HR HB. I was just an associated member in the staff of that operation, and the operation was led by General Blaskic, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So the answer to your question is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes. And in fact, when I see that -- we're going to go through some documents, but it appears that you were an associate member and that you were there to assist sort of in providing, you know, expertise in the sense of the knowledge that you have given your own background; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, in a way, but you should not understand this in the sense of -- that there weren't any professional people in the Main Staff. There were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand. No, I totally understand that, and I don't mean to minimise the professionality existed there, but it seemed that here the government was reaching out because of the nature because of this particular and complex issue. They were reaching out to folks like you to make sure that it was successful. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in we could go through some documents quickly 1D 01249, 1249. And this is a document that's signed by Jadranko Prlic as president, and as president of the government, although he seems to be called Prime Minister at times, but that's -- the correct translation should be president of government. It's dated 21 June 1994, and -- do you see that, sir? And if we look on page 2, at least in the English version page 2 and it might be page 2 for you as well, we see you are listed there as an associate member. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. We won't go through the entire document now because of time and because we'll have other opportunities through other witnesses to deal with this, Your Honours, but I just want to make sure that we get this information in. If we go on now to the next document, and that would be 1256, 1256, dated 24 June 1994. And this is, "Subject: Operation Spider," and in the very first paragraph it says: "Based on the approved plan of implementation of Operation Spider, Brigadier Marijan Biskic --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Karnavas. I'm a bit puzzled about the previous document. The only thing we have about it is that the witness's names figure there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If would you wait, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Oh.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's the whole point of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Then you went to the other document, so -- okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But, see, this is a chapter, and I tried to explain this to the legal officer, in fact, that if I was allowed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I wait. I wait.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I know, but this is a repeating issue, Your Honours. That's why I go from chapter to chapter. I alert everybody that I'm involved in a chapter. If you would just wait, a little bit of delayed gratification might be in order because at the end you will see. And then I want -- you can ask all the questions you want but I'm trying to at least help you out here, chapter -- you know, step-by-step.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Here we have -- we'll move on to the next document. We'll move on to the next document. It's getting impossible around here. 1251. 1251 seems to be meetings -- a meeting at the headquarters, again regarding Operation Spider. And here, sir, at the very beginning we see that you've taken the floor, and others speak as well, but do you see your name there, sir?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we go on to 1252. I apologise for not having the time to go through this, but we don't generally get a lot of time for our cross-examinations around here. Now, in this document it says: "General data on the perpetrators of a criminal act." And this -- this data seems at least when I glean at it, all relate to Operation Spider. Would that be correct? At the very top it should be operation -- is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And just by way of --

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It says, "Operation Spider."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. Now, if you look at -- just if you look at the first few names, you will see that the victims in -- these names, the victims are Muslims, are they not?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And the perpetrators seem to be Croatian names; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And this seems to be at least some verification that efforts were made, perhaps when conditions were more appropriate on the ground, to try to deal with some of the crimes that had been committed in the past; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then if we look at D -- 1D 1257. This is a letter that is sent to Mr. Gojko Susak. Now, maybe you know, maybe you don't know, but can you tell us why it was important or why was it necessary to inform Mr. Susak about this operation, other than the fact that perhaps Croatia was involved in providing some assistance to the local authorities to deal with this criminal activity?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember exactly what the reason for the report was. I assume there were two reasons. First one that I've already said, that Mr. Gojko Susak was highly interested in the situation in HR HB. And secondly, because at the request of the authorities of HR HB he gave permission for the crime prevention police to be aided and assisted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the -- just a couple of words about Operation Spider, and we're going to deal with this throughout -- later on in the course of this trial, but this was a rather sensitive operation, was it not?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And some of the individuals that were involved, that is the perpetrators, they -- some of them were rather dangerous, were they not?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, I don't have any further questions on this topic, Your Honours, if you wish to make any inquiries. Otherwise, I'll move to the next one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Before I move on to the next one, we saw -- Mr. Susak's name has come up a couple of times.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We would like to ask questions, but within your time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understand that, Mr. President. You have your own time, I have my time. I mean, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. We've heard -- we've heard Gojko Susak's name, and we all know who he was. We know that he came from Canada, but we also know that he hailed -- he was from Siroki Brijeg; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He had a house there and his mother lived down there at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Exactly. And that's the point I want to make, because that hasn't come out yet, that he had a house there and his mother lived there, that his mother lived there at that particular time, that period.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And she liked to play cards.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And he thinks he [sic] might have liked having her son come to visit her occasionally, or would that be somewhat unusual in the Croatian culture?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, you said that in this area you would not ask leading questions. I wonder whether you have changed your --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, now we're talking about Mr. Susak, and Mr. Susak has come up during the direct examination several times, and maybe we could -- we could do a search.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But, in fact, there were many questions from the Bench regarding Mr. Susak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And the whole issue is, occasionally Mr. Susak would come down and visit his mother, which is in Herzegovina; right?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that Mr. Susak came several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I know that. But it would -- but, see, here's the situation that we have here: The Prosecution there thinks that there is a joint criminal enterprise, and the reason that Mr. Susak came down was for criminal purposes, and here I'm asking you whether when he came down he came to visit his mother? And if he came to visit his mother, would it not be also natural for him to go out and maybe meet with others and for others to meet with him, given that he was, after all, the minister of defence of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you fully, and that's what I said myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke along those lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Well, we can move off Mr. Susak. And then I want to just deal with a very minor issue, nothing that important but one that I think needs some clarification, and that has to -- this deals with the -- the issue of language or the one terminology, because -- one term, because when we were -- looked at document 7155, 7155, this was a Prosecution document, it's been translated here in English as "prisoners of war." Now, if you could -- if we could -- now, if you look at the Croatian version, you use the word "zatocenik." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And this is again for the benefit of the Trial Chamber, because there was some -- there was a discussion on this. If we could look at 1D 01255. This is from a dictionary. It's a Croatian-English, English-Croatian dictionary, and there are two terms. If we look at the one that you used, and this would be found on -- at the top of the page, it's 1646, in English, at least, it says internee, detainee, confined person. Then it says captive person, prisoner, exile, banished person. That's the word that you -- that you used, correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat that, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if you look at page 1646, and this is more for the Court's benefit, we will find the word that you used. It's on the right-hand column, and under that it says internee, detainee. And as I understand your testimony, when you use that word you were referring to Muslims who had been in the HVO who were more or less -- I mean, there was -- for lack of a better term, this was an act of treason in a sense; correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. Okay, distinction --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay, if we look at the previous page, "zarobljenik," a term that you did not use but nonetheless it's in the dictionary, here we have captive, prisoner, prisoner of war, POW. So at least in the Croatian language, they do make a distinction between the two; correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and distinction is very important, and you've just explained it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And again, that was for the benefit of the Trial Chamber, and we can move on. Now, during -- you gave a statement to the Prosecution on two separate occasions. Is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in fact when I look at it seems they questioned you for about six days. Somewhere in the neighbourhood of that.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and after that for two more days. Eight days altogether.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in fact, it was a lot of reading. And one thing that struck me was that during that entire period you never refused to answer a question; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have told them everything I know, and if I know things why should I refuse to answer them? In the same way I have not refused to answer anything here. So it is correct that I have not refused to answer a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in fact, you -- you made the statement that you're neither ashamed of or afraid of the truth; correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's exactly what I said. I said that I was not afraid or ashamed of the truth, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And as far as -- and it would be fair to say that you stand by all of the answers to all of the questions that they posed to you?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the translation is good, then, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And in fact, those interviews were being tape recorded or videotaped, one of the two?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first six days, yes, and the last two days, which took place some fortnight ago, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And as I understand from reading it -- as far as I understand from reading the -- the statement, many of the questions that were posed to you here today and yesterday and the day before and what have you, were posed during those interviews, but during that period of time you had more of an opportunity to elaborate; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. And I also saw more documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I take it you would not have any objections to those -- your statement to come in to evidence, to be part of the evidence in addition to your testimony?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't object to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Very well. Now, I want -- the issue --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And by the way, Your Honours, we will be tendering, and I will go through a little bit of the statement, not much, but there are two documents. It's 1D 01258 and 1259. These are the documents, just for the record; I'm not going to go through them right now, but just so you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And, sir, there is no translation of it, but I just want to move on to the next topic, and this topic deals with the decision of the organisation of the Ministry of Defence. Now, do you recall being asked questions regarding that?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was asked questions about the decision on setting up the Ministry of Defence of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna of 18 December 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, as I understand it from reading it at least, you were asked several questions over several -- several pages, in fact, regarding that, and the first -- during the first day, and they did not show you the document themselves, the one dated 17 October -- I'm sorry, the one dated 18 December 1993. Do you recall that? And it wasn't until the following day, which would have been May 10, 1993, that you actually came in, and you pointed out to them and tried to explain to them how the -- how it was organised. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And I point this out for the Trial Chamber primarily, because it would appear that they're trying to get you to commit to something without even showing you the document, to at least try to have you give your interpretation of the document based on the reading of the law itself as opposed to trying to get you to guess. Now, if we could look at this document very briefly, it was shown to you yesterday, I believe, the Prosecution -- under the Prosecution's number it's 7236. If we could look at that for a second, and then I'm going to show you another document. 7236, if you -- you should have it there. This is a Prosecution document. Do you see it, sir?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And it's my upstanding that based on reading -- looking at this document, particularly if we look at -- I believe it's -- it was based on this document that you had indicated that the Main Staff is under the department of defence; is that correct? I believe it's Article 12. It says, "the chief of the Main Staff shall be responsible to the minister of defence for matters of general organisation and functioning in the peacetime and wartime." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then if we look at Article 13, it says: "The chief of the Main Staff is directly responsible to the president of the republic in all matters of Supreme Command, organisation, strategic and operative matters, and use of armed forces in peace and war"; correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct, and exactly how I said at the time and explained things at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. And it was -- it was after you showing them this article you answered their question that the president of the government, you know, was not responsible -- or was not the superior of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct. And I also said that we had to look at the previous decision which was annulled by the subsequent decision. I did not see the previous one, but I believe that it was similar to the later one. I said in answer to the question that while I was there that decision was enforced, and I also reminded the Prosecutor that they should look at the decision dated 15 December 1992, which was superseded by the subsequent decision.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And the interpreter corrects the date: 15 September 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I just so happen to have that document, and if we look at P 00586. And again for the Court's -- for the Court, for the Trial Chamber to consider, the gentleman is being questioned on May 9th and 10th of 2005. So query whether the Prosecution at the time, or at least the individuals questioning him, were aware of these documents and what the documents contained therein, and query why they didn't show these documents to the gentleman. But if we look at this particular one, and I think we might have touched on this yesterday, under IV, at least it talks about, the head of the department of defence will have deputies. V talks about the deputy head of security. We covered that. But then if we go on to IX. In the English version it would be on page 5, and it's page 3 for you. And again I raise this because this seems to be a continuing issue in this trial, and here we are almost 10 months into it and we have yet to resolve it. Now, under IX, it says that the Main Staff of the Croatian Defence Council shall be part of the department. And then it goes on. Now, if we look further down in the -- under IX it says: "The chief of the Main Staff shall be directly responsible to the president of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna for all issues relating to the Supreme Command, unit organisation, strategic and operative plans, and the use of the armed forces in time of war and peace." And just as you had indicated that probably the previous document was similar to the one that you brought to their attention, we see that the language is identical, do we not, sir?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When it comes to the chief the Main Staff to whom he reported, and when it comes to superior command, strategic planning, and the use of the armed forces, both in wartimes and times of peace.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, I don't wish to go into that too much because others may want to cover in more detail the other aspects, with respect to what the minister of defence can or cannot do, but anyway, I just wanted to point that out because, at least during the interview, it appeared they were trying to say that Mr. Prlic was responsible to the armed force -- or for the armed forces. Now, incidentally when you were questioned on May 10th -- I mean, on May 9th, I'm sorry, you said that you had never received a verbal or a written order from Jadranko Prlic. On that would be on page 19, Your Honours, starting with the transcript of May 9th, and it's 5 -- it's 1D 01258. Anyway, I point that out. You were being asked if you received orders from Jadranko Prlic and you indicated that neither an oral nor written order was received by you from Dr. Jadranko Prlic. Do you stand by that answer, sir?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. We'll move on. Next topic. And this may be my very last one, Your Honours, so ... Now, a little bit about the organisation of the government, because I think this again ties in with what we've been talking about. Incidentally, did they ever show you any documents with respect to how the -- the government was structured, how the -- from the Presidency to the -- the executive authority when it was HZ HB versus when it became HR HB? Did they show you any documents?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And of course you're not lawyer by training. We'll agree on that; right?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But this line of questioning sort of deals with the issue of who appointed you, because -- and again, this is a matter that needs to be cleared up. Hopefully we'll never have to deal with this again. I doubt it, but we probably will, because there's an insistence that it was Jadranko Prlic who appointed you because we see his signature there, that he personally appointed you. This seems to be the issue, and I want to clarify this. If we could look at document -- we'll start off with 5813, 5813. This is from Official Gazette, and now I'm dealing with the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna. And here he -- it says here in Article 2 that the government consists of the Prime Minister. We submit that this is a wrong interpretation. It should be president of government. Deputy ministers, ministers, and other ministers. If we look at Article 3, second paragraph, it says: "The Prime Minister, deputy -- deputy Prime Ministers and members of the government are jointly responsible for decisions made by the government and are particularly responsible for their own field of work." Do you see where it says they're jointly responsible for the decisions made by the government, sir? Do you see that part? That's on Article 3. Not that important.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you asking me?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we move to Article 17, and again I'm going to move through several documents just to clarify a point. It's unfortunate I have to do it through you and not through somebody else, but it's something we continually have to struggle here with. Article 17, and again there is a mistranslation and we will be asking for an official translation, for the first line, that is, where it says, "the Prime Minister shall appoint," it actually should be the president of the government shall convene a session. Not appoint the government but convene a session. Basically that's what it's talking about. And if we look at the last paragraph within Article 17, it says: "The Prime Minister shall sign regulations and other acts passed by the government and make sure that they are implemented." So here it says -- here it gives us the reasoning why it's Jadranko Prlic who is signing the document, which are decisions that are jointly made by the government, not his decisions. Do you see that, sir? Okay.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. We'll move on quickly. If we go on to the next document, 6995, 6995. This is a decision. It's dated 20 November 1993, and this says that: "The Chamber of Deputies of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna at its 3rd session held on 20 November 1993, issued the following decision," and here we see where Dr. Jadranko Prlic is appointed as president of the government, as well as all the other ministers. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, we go on to 1D 01260, and this is dated 4 May 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But, Your Honours, if you look at the first paragraph under "Decree," it talks about a session that was held on 20 November 1993. So even though this was signed by President Zubak at the time, it was based on a session that was held on 20th November 1993. And I want to look at two articles from this, Articles 26 and 29, because this -- we're getting to you, sir, slowly but surely. It talks about Article 26. It says: "The ministries are managed by the ministers. The minister has a deputy minister," and it goes on. Now, if we go to Article 29: "Managing employees at the ministries, offices, and administrations are ..." So this is a definitional article. "The managing employees are at the ministries' assistant minister," at the very top one, and then it lists the other ones, the offices, and so on. Then if we go on to the following paragraph, it says: "Managing employees at the republic administration bodies and the republic's administration organisations are appointed and relieved of duty by the government, at the minister's proposal." And again, this is for the Trial Chamber's benefit because it shows who appoints, who relieves. That it's not an individual, but it's a government -- it's a collective decision. Now, do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, if we go on -- we're coming to you now, sir, slowly. If we look at 699 -- 6994. And this is a decision. It's signed by Jadranko Prlic, and this is where everybody gets confused. Because it's signed they automatically assumed that he's the one that appoints, he's the one that fires, and therefore he is the one that direct controls and has the effective command and control over the individuals. And here, this is a decision for your appointment, do you see that, sir? 6994. Decision appointing you as assistant minister.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now -- now for the finale on this issue because it helps us a little bit. Let's step back a moment in time and let's look at the extract of the minutes of the meeting, and this would be document -- Prosecution document 7000, 7000. Again, it may seem like a minor, inconsequential point, but this is why I was up in arms with respect to command and control earlier in the week. This is from 1 December 1993. Now, if we look at --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: On the English version it would be page 12, Your Honours, under item 21.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: For you, sir, it's page 8. It will be page 8 in Croatian. It's page 12 for us in English. And we see here in the third paragraph on page 12, I will read it slowly: "The deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Defence Perica Jukic proposed appointing Brigadier Miljenko Crnjac from Siroki Brijeg as deputy minister of defence, and Colonel Marijan Biskic from Derventa, and Mayor Dusan Vir from Livno, as assistant ministers of defence for security and political activity respectively. The government approved the proposals for assistant ministers of defence, and the deputy's to be appointed bit Chamber of Deputies of the Assembly of the HR HB." Now, sir, correct me if I'm wrong. Does it not look like from these minutes, dovetailed by what the law said earlier and what the decision says later, that you were proposed by the minister, and it was the government that approved that proposal?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I was always clear on that. There was nothing unclear to me in that respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. And based on that approval of the -- of the government, a decision was made which was signed by Jadranko Prlic, and hopefully this clarifies the matter as to whether Jadranko Prlic appointed you personally and, therefore, had command and control over you, or whether this was an effort by the government based on a proposal by the minister himself for your services. Sir, I have nothing further at this point in time. I have nothing further to question you on. I want that thank you very, very much for coming here. It's been an honour and privilege to have you here in this courtroom?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, you can have the rest of my time if you have any questions, otherwise I will yield my time to my colleague, Ms. Nozica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a clarification, please, Mr. Karnavas. I would like to know something about Operation Spider. In the documents in B/C/S, there are some 40 documents which establish that certain individuals committed crimes, but there are only eight translations. It -- is it the fact that you did not have the time to translate all the documents or did you make a decision what to translate, whatnot?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you for that question. I appreciate that question, Mr. President. Here is the problem: The translation services in this Tribunal certainly do not operate in a convenient time for the Defence. You need months and months in advance to propose something for them, and it takes literally hours and hours just to get one page transcribed because of the bureaucracy. So we do internal translations, and for those it -- we're just stretched. So we do not have -- we also moved to have a translator assigned to us, as we're entitled for certain matters. That has not occurred. The request has been in for almost a month now, if not longer than that. So we apologise. It wasn't that we made a choice and we're trying to cherry pick. It's just the we -- I wanted to give you a flavour, and, of course, as I indicated, in due time we will discuss Operation Spider more thoroughly, and we can have all the documents translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, I'll give you the floor, but just before that, for the transcript, 1D 01052 [as interpreted], will certainly be tendered into evidence. Now, concerning the documents translated into English, I'd like to say for the transcript, I'd like to mention three names. There's Tihomir Buric, aka Spiko. That's a name we've already heard, so I'd like to draw attention to that. Then there's another name that appears in this list, and that is Mladen Naletilic, aka Tuta, who is also mentioned, and a third person who is mentioned, and he might be of relative importance that was raised for April 1993 in Ahmici. So that is what I wanted to say. Mr. Mundis, you were on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours, and everyone in and around the courtroom. Just three very, very quick points before the break. The first one perhaps Judge Trechsel or others may want to look during the break. I know Mr. Karnavas was making reference to Prosecution Exhibit P 07798. You will recall that's the document that apparently had a missing cover page. As we informed the Defence last week, P 07796, which is in the Prosecution bundle, contains the same document that's in P 07798 and includes the covering letter. So for the record, P 07798 is totally encompassed by P 07796, which is a more complete version of that document, for the record. Second, it would appear as though the Prlic Defence team will be tendering the entire transcripts of the prior interviews with this witness. I should note for the record that during those six days of interviews that took place in 2005 the witness was shown a substantial number of documents. I'm not sure if the Prlic Defence team intends on tendering the documents that the witness was shown during those interviews, but I will state for the record that in the event they do not do that the Prosecution very well may seek leave to have documents admitted into evidence on the basis of those earlier interviews in which the witness explains and comments on those documents, and I simply want to put that out there so that the Prlic Defence can take that into consideration, but if they're tendering the transcripts, we will review those transcripts to determine if additional documents could or should be tendered as a result of those earlier interviews. And finally, today being international women's day, we would be remiss if we didn't note that. I know it's a very important holiday in the Balkans. It perhaps should be given more weight elsewhere, but I would like to wish all of our female colleagues happy international women's day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very briefly. There was a correction on line -- page 39, line 2. It should be 1252 as opposed to -- I believe it reads now 1052. It should say 1252. And I understand, Mr. Mundis's observations with regards to the transcript. Obviously I -- we did take that into consideration, and that would be standard practice. So -- and I totally agree with his approach. It should be 1D 1252.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak, you're on your feet.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If Your Honours grant permission and if Ms. Senka Nozica stays for some time, then there's some technical questions that can better be clarified with an educated and well-versed witness. That's the first point. And secondly, leave the Balkans alone. We're from Croatia, from Bosnia-Herzegovina. We're not a collection of Balkan people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please. Yes, Counsel Alaburic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In view of the fact that Mr. Praljak said something that I was going to ask for at the beginning of today's proceedings, and that is to be given 10 minutes for additional cross-examination of this witness, because I consider that this witness is exceptionally --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please. Additional time -- for additional time you'll have to wait. You had a fixed amount of time. Counsel Nozica has 75 minutes, and that is what I'm preoccupied with to begin with. We'll see about all the rest afterwards. So the priority is to allow Counsel Nozica 75 minutes, especially if there are procedural matters and so on. So let's look at priorities first. Ms. Nozica will go first. But before that, we have a question from our Judge. Yes, Counsel Alaburic, I've taken note of what your concerns are.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the Court's permission, may I just thank Mr. Mundis for his greetings and good wishes, and we from the Balkans always considered the 8th of March, Women's Day, to be a democratic heritage and that it is marked in the same way in democratic countries.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I am not using the time for the same. I have a question for the witness which concerns the document 1D 01248. I'm not sure that you have to look at it. You will recall that it is a document where, I think, you gave the order that certain investigations be undertaken. Now, I would like to know whether any results have been generated by these investigations into alleged crimes. Can you inform the Chamber about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for the question. I issued the order on the 29th of March, 1994. I cannot now remember the concrete results. However, quite certainly there were some results which were recorded in the military police administration of the Croatian Defence Council and the SIS administration as well, and similarly the results of this order can be viewed from the -- from Operation Spider that we mentioned a moment ago, from that aspect as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. I note that you speculate. You say "quite certainly," "most probably," but you cannot specifically answer in the positive or in the negative.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said, Your Honour, that I cannot speak about concrete cases because you must understand that almost seven years have gone by since then, but I'm quite convinced that this order started to be complied with and that I'm sure there were some results and that these would be found either on the side of the Defence or the Prosecution, that they would find some record of results.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In fairness to the witness, you know, the question should be: Was he asked to look for or did the Prosecution search for, because I think had he -- or if he had been aware that such a question might be posed, maybe he could have tried to locate documents. And again the burden is on the Prosecution to show that those documents don't exist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. President -- Mr. Karnavas, I put this question, and I do not stand to be corrected. I think it was quite correct to put it the way I put it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Okay. I have a question to you, Mr. Karnavas. On page 29, lines 18 to 22, you make an observation regarding the Chamber that I'm not quite sure I understand correctly, and I would like you to explain what you mean by it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What's the observation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: You said -- sorry, I'm just finding it. "I point this out for the Trial Chamber primarily because it would appear that they're trying to get you to commit to something without even showing you the document, to at least try to have you give your interpretation of the document based on the reading of the law."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I accept. It was "they" being -- obviously the record doesn't reflect my hand motioning to "they" being the Prosecution, not the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I was -- that's what I wanted to hear, because it was strange. It looked -- it sounded very strange.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And it sounds on the record, but it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Your explanation is taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. Because if you put it in context, they were the ones who were questioning them and they did not show him the documents, and it would seem to me that if you were going to question somebody for six days and you're asking him to speculate, show him the documents and let him interpret. That was the -- so there was no implication that the Trial Chamber is in any way trying to trick a witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. That's what I wanted to hear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're going to take a 20-minute break and reconvene in 20 minutes' time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hearing is resumed. Before I give the floor to Counsel Nozica, the Chamber would like to ask the Prosecution, so Mr. Mundis, listen carefully. We're going to speak to Mr. Scott later on. We'd like to ask the Prosecution to furnish as soon as possible a provisional chart of witnesses or timetable for witnesses that you consider hearing between now and the end of the trial. So we'd like a list of all the witnesses, and also the names of the witnesses who are not going to come, those that you have decided not to call. So we'd like those too. And I personally need to have this schedule for me to be able to respond to your motion for appeal. I think that, if I remember correctly, the Prosecution said they would make a general schedule, and we never actually received a complete timetable. So if you say that you don't have enough time, that's fine, but we'd like to have a timetable to see where we're going and how much more there is left. You did this kind of timetable for April, so May, June, July, September. Would you put your witnesses within that timetable, and tell us which witnesses you do not intend to call so that if need be the Trial Chamber can call them, if they deem necessary. Have you understood that, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Absolutely, Mr. President. I can assure the Trial Chamber that we are in fact in the process of doing that, and I cannot at this point commit in terms of when we might have such a timetable available, but I would expect it would be in the very near future, and we -- we are working on that as expeditiously as possible. As we've indicated before, a number of the remaining witnesses, being what might be called international witnesses, are a little bit more difficult to schedule than some of the crime base witnesses, and we are, to be as transparent as possible, encountering some difficulty in scheduling some of those witnesses, particularly as we move into the summer period, but we are working on that, and I will redouble our efforts in order to provide you with that. I believe we can certainly provide a list of witnesses that we don't intend to call, and the timetable we will provide as soon as possible, and with the caveat, of courses, that it -- that there could be parts of it that are provisional, and that there could be parts of it that have yet to be confirmed or even yet to be filled in. Certain -- we have a couple of week periods where we have no witnesses scheduled yet, but I will endeavour to provide all that information as quickly as that as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
