utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. In order to be precise, following on from what you said, we need the names of witnesses that you're not going to call. That's the first point. And secondly, and I completely agree with you, that there are witness whom you have difficulty bringing in, to know what month, when, but you must make an approximation, because what we want to know is how many more witnesses you're going to call, which will allow us to compare this to the time and the 65 ter list and so on. So we need this timetable. And I need it personally so that I can rule.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I completely understand that, Mr. President, and I neglected to mention, of course, one other factor that as we move into some of the more what we again colloquially might call linkage type of witnesses, such as the current witness, there are -- there are periods of time where we will only anticipate calling one witness per week. So the number of witnesses once we finish the Vares component towards the end of March, that the number of witnesses will dramatically go down in terms of our ability to call more than six or perhaps seven witnesses in an entire month because of the fact that they tend to be much more lengthy witnesses. So the overall number of witnesses after March is not a large number compared to the crime base witnesses where we could do two or three such witnesses in one day. So I will flag that up for the Chamber. But I do understand, and we will get that information to Your Honours as quickly as we possibly can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And just something else. The Chamber has deliberated the matter and decided that during the holidays -- or, rather, during the summer break that we're going to be working in the first week of July, and we'll continue on the 7th of August. You have 75 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I'd like to inform you that my binders are with the registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to say good afternoon to the witness. Good afternoon, Mr. Biskic. And I'd like to inform you and Their Honours, the witness Prosecutor, that in my black binder, Mr. Biskic, there are exhibits which the Prosecutor showed this witness, and they have pink stickers on them. This will allow the Judges to find their way in my set, in my binder. So I had good intentions. Those were upset a bit because I think that we need to clarify one point for the record. May we have on e-court, to save the witness from looking for it, Exhibit 7236. It's not in my binder, unfortunately. I didn't know that I would be needing it. It's P 07236, and it is a Prosecution exhibit which was presented to the witness, and a moment ago while my colleague, Mr. Karnavas, conducted the cross-examination the witness looked at the document too. Mr. Biskic, it's the decision on the basis for the organisation of the Ministry of Defence. Do you have the Prosecution binder to hand? No, you don't. Very well. Well, you have it on e-court, on the screen. Can we take a look at the last page of this decision. For the witness, may we have the last page. That's right. Thank you. Now, let's take a look, and I'm doing this for the transcript more than for your own testimony, at point -- Article 20. It says: "The decisions on the foundation of the organisation of the department of defence, number 599/92, of the 15th of September, 1992, is no longer in effect, is null and void." Let us now --

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let's have a look at another exhibit shown to the witness twice. It is P 00586. Just to have a look at the date for us to establish whether the decision shown to the witness was the decision that was declared null and void. P 00586. We just need the first page, and it will explain everything to us. This is a decision of the 17th of October, 1992; is that right? It's obvious. You can see the date at the top.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And it says: "Please find attached the decision on the foundations of organisation signed by Mr. Bruno Stojic."

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we have a look at the last page of that decision now, please. Do we see that it says the 17th of October, 1992, on the last page too? Whereas here it says the 15th of September, and that was the reason why I wanted to put that right. In P 00586, it is not a decision of the 17th of October, 1992, but it is a decision of the 15th of September, 1992. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Then we can move on. Mr. Biskic, when you arrived in Herceg-Bosna, you did not occupy a post of the head of the defence department -- or you did not come across Bruno Stojic when you arrived, did you?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: After that, did you have any contact with him?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that in November Mr. Bruno Stojic was away attending a meeting in Mr. Jukic's office as advisor for production, and he did not appear after that, and I think that that was placed outside the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. We're talking about the period of time when you began working in the Ministry of Defence to reorganise the security sector; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if you're talking about the beginning of -- well, if you're talking about the beginning of December, I had no contacts, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Your task and assignment was to establish the proper functioning of the Ministry of Defence in the government of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in a way, yes, but not to establish the Ministry of Defence, just a part of the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So you're referring to the security sector, the SIS, and the military police; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that this reorganisation was necessary precisely in order to change the entire system, because executive power and authority up until then in the HR HB was provisional, and now a new stage was beginning whereby the ministries were to be established instead of the previous departments?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I agree with what you said, although I can't say whether the previous one was provisional or not, but the answer is yes because everything was changing or being changed.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes. I think that is incontestable, that these were provisional parts up until that time. So as you're undertaking a new -- the construction of a new system, was that the reason for which you did not determine the structure that existed before your arrival, but you knew part of it?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I have a bit of a problem when you say you could say yes. I don't know what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said that I didn't deal with the past, and one of the reasons, of course, was that the -- had the same system remained, then I would have had to study that previous system, so that you could say yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I see. Thank you. Your explanations are very important, and whenever you feel the need to explain everything, please feel free to do so. After your arrival, there was a reorganisation in the HVO, and I'm thinking about its military structure.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It was only upon your arrival after a certain amount of time had gone by that you, among other things, among other tasks, were given the assignment of disbanding the detainee centres.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: According to the documents that we've seen so far over the past three days, in implementing that task, you received authorisation to coordinate with all the structures within HR HB. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you could put it that way, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'll explain where I get that conclusion from. At the meetings that you organised, the representatives of all the bodies of HR HB were present, from the presidential offices or cabinet of HR HB to representatives of most of the ministries?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But a moment ago when I said you could put it that way, I wasn't the main person at the meeting, because the minister also attended as did other people who occupied higher positions than myself. But in a way I was the operational man.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'll just enumerate who was involved in all this. There were commissions that were established by HR HB, were there not?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Or representatives of individual ministries; right?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Biskic, I said that you were the coordinator.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You could put it that way, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes. You were the coordinator. Now, to make things quite clear, this task did not come under the authority of the Ministry of Defence in which you were the assistant security minister?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was an assignment of all the bodies involved in HR HB, and outside that, the institutions of the International Red Cross, the office for displaced persons and refugees, and similar institutions.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You came to the position of assistant minister for security by appointment on the 1st of December, 1993. Can we confirm that once again?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Before being officially appointed, you started collecting information about where prisoners of war were being held and in what centres and who headed those centres. Am I right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: According to the documents that we have in our possession, you started your activities before an official decision had been taken by the president of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, Mr. Boban, and several times you expressed the wish to see that document, so I'm going to show it to you now, but do you agree with me that you started your activities before his decision was officially made public?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Were you informed by the presidential cabinet of the HR HB that such a decision was being prepared, so that's why you started acting eight away?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know about the decision, but quite simply, as I got to know the situation, I set certain steps in motion to resolve some of the problems.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Boban, as president of the HR HB, issued an order on the unconditional disbanding of detainee centres on the territory of HR HB on the 10th of December, 1993. So I'd now like to ask you to take a look at document number, in my binder, and it should be marked in yellow, it is 7096. And I'd just like to inform you that the numbers are in order. So it's 7096. P 07096 is the number of the document, and the documents follow each other in consecutive order.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We can see that the decision was made on the 10th of December, 1993. Mr. Boban refers to certain agreements, and the Geneva agreement is one the most important ones, as well as the declaration on human rights, and he says that all detainee centres should be disbanded on the territory of the Republic of Herceg-Bosna unconditionally. From this decision --

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: From this decision, and I'm going to ask you simple questions, we can see that the decision is being made by the president of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: From this decision we can also see that most probably before this decision was taken he knew that on the territory of HR HB there were detainee centres; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the assumption, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let's go a little further than just mere assumption. In order to make a decision of this kind there must have been knowledge about what you were deciding on; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This decision is one by the president, so it is a political decision which, as a rule, only the president can make based on his competence and authority. You can assume that, and then we'll see that that is indeed so in due course, but do you agree with me that these are political decisions taken by, let's use a term that might not be appropriate in this courtroom, but which is a sovereign decision? He makes sovereignly. He decides to disband unconditionally these prisons and that people be set at liberty. Can you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'm saying this because we have had an opportunity to see such decisions in the course of these proceedings. Such decisions have been taken by President Boban and the president of the Presidency, Alija Izetbegovic. These were the two people who such decisions. Not even members of the Presidency, although the president is only the first among equals. Those decisions were taken for the territories that they were irrespectively in charge of, and later on the decisions were implemented by those who were authorised by these two to implement them. Do you know anything about that? Do you know anything about some previous decisions? Were there any agreements, international accords after which similar decisions would follow?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of such decisions, but I believe that there must have been such decisions even before this one. And let me just tell you that this is the first time I see this decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: When you were interviewed by the Prosecutor, you said on several occasions that you had never seen this decision. That's why I'm showing it to you today, to show you what it looks like. Could you also tell me this: I believe that you have two wars behind you, one in Bosnia-Herzegovina, the other in Croatia, and I'm sure you can answer the following question: Can we then conclude that such decisions, decisions on disbanding certain centres are within the exclusive authority of the president of a state or the president of an entity? When I say "entity," I'm saying this because at the moment when the decision was made, the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna was an entity, because if we look at this decision taken by Mr. Boban above the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, it says "Bosnia-Herzegovina," which means that the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna was one part or an entity in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Can we then conclude that such decisions are within the exclusive authority of the presidents, the presidents of the Presidency, or those who are authorised to lead the state or an entity?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't answer your are question fully, but I believe that if he took this decision that it must have been within his purview as the president of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Let's go back to something that you know much better, and this is your operative work on the implementation of this decision. You've already told us that after you collected some information about the detainee centres that had existed at the time when you arrived in the territory of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, you received information that the prisons in Heliodrom and Ljubuski were secured by the military police. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was in the report of the acting chief of the police administration of the HR -- HVO. The date is 22nd of November, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In the course of your work were you aware of who had taken the decision on the establishment of the central prison in Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw this decision. I don't know who had passed it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So you don't know when this decision was passed?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You then also don't know which of the facilities among those that you saw at Heliodrom was the central military prison. Wouldn't I be right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you would.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let's clarify this. You don't know who brought people in, how, which categories of people, when were people brought to the central military police? Wouldn't that be correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it would. I've already said that I have never been provided with a full answer to that question by anybody.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: As for the prison in Gabela, you were informed that the security, and I'm being very precise -- precise here, I'm not talking about anybody's authorities, I'm just talking about providing security, and for that prison the security was provided by the home guards?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did you also establish there were prisons in police that had been established by certain brigades - and let me just finish - that were secured by members of the brigade military police?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I learnt that later on when I was implementing the decision by the president of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna. And this referred to the area of Rama.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I remember that you said that yesterday, but I don't think that it made its way to the record. That's why I went back to this. Did you also establish that there were prisons that were secured by MUP members?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in Livno and Tomislavgrad.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Did you also establish that there were some private prisons, and "private" in quotation marks?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In some units.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in certain reports, Vojno was mentioned which was never treated as an accommodation facility for a -- prisoners, detainees, or anybody else.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let me show you a document, which is very significant, in my view. This document is number P 08077. I don't know whether you have ever seen it before. I don't think you did. You were talking about this situation and you couldn't remember something. Did you find it?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's 077.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is a letter to the chief of the Main Staff -- actually, by the chief the Main Staff, Mr. Roso, dated 16th March, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I don't have the time and it is not my goal to do this but I can tell you that this is actually a reaction by Mr. Roso to the information that he had received about Vojno that we saw within document -- document P 07798 that you were questioned a lot about by the Trial Chamber, and the questions were to the effect whether Mr. Jukic reacted, whether Mr. Roso reacted, and now we see a reaction of that sort here in this letter; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Have you ever seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because at the time I was absent, but you can see that it was sent to the administration of the SIS as well as the administration of the police. I myself never saw it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Under item 1 it -- there is a mention of private prisons, and at the time Mr. Roso reacted about information -- to the information about Vojno. There are certain number of MOS members in private prisons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yesterday, we spoke at length about the chain of command, about the line of command. Look at the way General Roso as the chief of the Main Staff gives a task to the SIS administration and the police administration. Can you look at that, please?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Those are the situation when the chief of the Main Staff can issue orders to certain sectors in the ministry and in the Ministry of Defence, and we will also see a reverse situation, if we have the time. In your view, sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Just a question, Witness. You have said with regard to this document that you had never seen it, but you know that it refers to Vojno. How do you know this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I assume because General Roso refers to the facts that he was provided by the Red Cross and the High Commissioner. And these were the same letters were sent to us, some of them addressed to General Roso.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: And they refer to Vojno, these letters.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that based on -- pursuant to the lawyer's question, I said yes, and then finally I said that I assume this was the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In order to clarify this, can we show in e-court P 07798. I'm afraid, Your Honours, you don't have it in hard copy. This is the document speaking about the information relative to Vojno. I apologise. Just a moment, please bear with me.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This was the previous document. Can the Prosecutor help me, please. This is P 7787, and now it is marked as P 07798. This is in the transcript, and this is the information that you were talking about.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said that I assume that a link could be made between the letter by the International Committee of the Red Cross or in the letter by General Roso in which he gives the task to the administration of the SIS and the military police.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Correct. And you can see that date on the letter the 3rd February, 1994. Isn't that correct? You can see it on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You can see it on the English version since you don't have the B/C/S version. I would like to dwell upon these private prisons. I believe that based on your military experience both in Croatia and in Bosnia-Herzegovina you know that these were -- these were common situations that certain units would organise their private prisons, and those would function until the moment somebody learnt about them and asked them to do something about them. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say that this was a common occurrence. They were isolated occurrences, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I did not say common occurrences referring to a certain locality. When I said "common occurrences," I am saying that this happened in all units in all the militaries in Bosnia-Herzegovina. I am referring to three militaries that were present there, and I am also implying the Croatian army. That's why I said that this was frequent, although I know that these were isolated cases.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can talk about Bosnia-Herzegovina and say yes, but I can't remember any such thing in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Croatia is not the topic of our conversation today at all. Let's then sum up and say that you established that the prisons or certain prisons were under the control of or under the security of members of both military and civilian structures, and we can conclude that based on the analysis that we have just done.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We may say that if you imply the Ministry of the Interior when you say civilian structures. If we're talking about private prisons, I don't know what you mean by civilian structures.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Exactly what you've just said. I know that if a unit has its own private prison then this is not a civilian structure. So your answer is exactly what I was expecting from you. You established who provided security for certain prisons, but you didn't establish within which -- within whose purview they were, within whose authority. Am I right in saying this?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right. I've already answered that question, and I have already told you that to this very day I don't know under whose authority they were, which ministry within which institution.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: By a decision dated 8 December 1993, you determined for the military prisons in Ljubusko a company commander that would provide security. Stanko Bozic was that commander; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In other words, these two centres, when it came to their security they were under the authority of the Ministry of Defence of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And those centres to which civilians were transferred after this date were under the authority of the civilian authorities. Am I right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that. I could only state what was regulated by my decision. And if this is an inference you can make, then I can say yes, but I cannot state that for a fact because I was not in charge of that part.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I have asked you about your authorities as the coordinator of the entire activity, and since some of your decisions went beyond the authorities that you had in the Ministry of Defence, I ascribe them to your capacity as the coordinator.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just one explanation. My decision that was issued on the 8th, this was not my coordination role but my role as the assistant minister, because the accommodation facility in Heliodrom and the prison in Ljubuski were provided with clear authority when it came to the military police security. This was not done in my role as a coordinator but as an assistant minister.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: If you'll allow me, we'll come to that, but on the 8th of December you did not issue an order, did you?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was not an order. It was a letter.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, we will -- we'll see if this was an order or not, but I believe this was within the regulations.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You're saying that you don't know who had authority over civilian prisons, i.e., whether the civilians who were not in Ljubuski and Heliodrom were under the authority of civilian authorities, and you said you didn't know. What civilians are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about the time when the definition was established as to who prisoners of war were.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: But this was not on the 8th?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about at the time when that definition was made, the definition of the prisoners of war. They were placed in Heliodrom and in the prison in Ljubuski.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We established that they could remain in prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And who went to Gabela?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those who to be exchanges or who were to go to the third countries, and the fourth group were those who were released in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina. From then on Gabela became a transit centre which was under the authority of the International Committee of the Red Cross, the service for exchanges, when it came to the implementation of the decision.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is exactly why I asked you whether this was under the authority of civilian institutions, because the implementation of that task was in the hands of the civilian institutions. I hope that we would understand each other when I said that.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: On the 20th of December, 1993, you passed an instruction about the treatment of prisoners of war in which you stated obligations. This was a regulation or an instruction how to treat prisoners of war, and you stated what the obligations of the members of those who took prisoners of war were, as well as the warden and the staff employed at such centres it, as well as the obligations of the judiciary with regard to these individuals, i.e., the judges and the prosecutor. Can then one say that the authority over the newly established centres or accommodation facilities of prisoners of war were -- was in the hands of both the Ministry of Defence but also of the other ministries as, for example, the Ministry of Justice?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Ministry of Defence, the Ministry of Justice, and also the Ministry of Health, in the sense of health care.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I asked you this because of an observation you made in a letter to Mr. Susak on the 7th of December, 1993, and that is Prosecution Exhibit - it's got a pink sticker - P 07064.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You've found it. Very well. Now, I'm going to read that sentence out, and briefly could you explain it to us, because I think that there is a little contradiction there. This is what you say: "From the very beginning of the shelter," and I'd like to tell you that it is page 2 -- or, rather, paragraph 2 of page 1. "From the very time that the POW shelter was formed, as well as the collection centres, an organisational shortcoming was made without legal foundations. Everything was placed under the authority of the Ministry of Defence of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, although that should not have been the way it should be done."

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can accept what you say. I probably said that on the basis of the fact that at that moment in time the pressure, exclusive pressure to disband it all came from the Ministry of Defence of HR HB. And secondly, from the letter by the head of the administration or the acting head of the military police administration of the 17th of November, 1993, it says that security should be provided by the Home Guards Unit, and I considered that that, too, was part of the Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes. You're talking about the Home Guards Unit, which was a military unit and which belonged to the HVO. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I hope it belong to the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, we're not going to guess. There's no need to do that. We can establish that through witnesses who know that for certain. But anyway, we have seen and you said a number of times, so we have your testimony, too, that this observation of yours -- well, you say that everything came under the competence of the Ministry of Defence, which wasn't quite correct. We see that something came under the competence of MUP too.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. This is one month after my arrival, and so I allow for the possibility that there were certain incorrect things there, but I said on what basis I made those conclusions at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I can see that in fact almost all the information that you received from Mr. Lavric's letter, that's -- they all come from Mr. Lavric's report of the 22nd of November, which is P 06805, exhibit, and I'm sure you know it off by heart by now, but we can take a look at it nonetheless. That's where you got the information from. So what you wrote to Mr. Susak, in part you rely -- or in greater part you rely on this other letter; is that right? On this report.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On information from the 22nd of November to the 7th of December.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I just wanted to look at this in chronological order and to explain matters in that light, because I think the situation will be much clearer that way. After this report which you sent or the letter you sent to Mr. Susak, you compiled a letter, a communication dated the 8th of December, 1993. Would you look at P 07075 now, please.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What number did you say? 7075, is that it?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes. It's in fact a letter we've already seen where you refer to Mr. Bozic and the military police and the security to be provided by -- for Heliodrom and Ljubuski.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, I noticed here, and I think it would be a good idea for you to explain this to us. You observe here that you establish a security company to provide security for the POW shelter at Heliodrom and the military investigation prison of Ljubuski. So you didn't consider Ljubuski to be a shelter. Is that the difference that we're making here?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And everybody should make a difference between the POW shelter and the military investigation prison, because members of the HVO could be found in the military investigation prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I see, so that -- members of who?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Members of the Croatian Defence Council against whom legal proceedings are being taken.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And what about members of the BH army, if they had committed some crimes or offences?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, if they had committed offences and are under criminal investigation.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I consider this to be a recommendation for this situation to be regulated, and the order was issued by Mr. Lavric?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please slow down and not overlap. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise to the interpreters. I'll slow down. May we have Exhibit P 07098.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Could you tell me when you find that document? Let me know, please. P 07098. You've found it. Right.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is an order by the acting head of the military police on the basis of my letter of the 8th.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We're dealing with the 10th of December now; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, since this is an order, and the order has the same structure as your letter, as your other communication, but why is it being sent to the military district of Mostar and the defence of the town of Mostar, as it says below? It says, "Sent to."

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is the first time that I see this order, and I really can't answer that. I don't know. Maybe for logistical support, because I believe that -- well, I don't know for sure, but I can only assume that logistic support went through the logistic bodies of the military district of Mostar, but that is just my assumption.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Take a look at point 5. Can it have anything to do with the people that it's being sent to -- or, rather, at that time --

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Point 5 emanates from my own communication, from my own letter, and then the head of the administration raises that point again, which I think is quite in order.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. If you can't tell us that's fine. I wondered if you could tell it us whether during that time certain prisoners were being taken away to perform labour by these units, but if you don't know anything about that, we won't belabour the point.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean from the military district of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes, and the defence of the town of Mostar, too.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, although there's another very interesting area, I don't think I'll have time to go into that, so let's finish off with this. On the 13th of December, 1993, you issue an order.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And may I have the next document on e-court, please, P 07149.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Tell me when you've found it.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: By this order you determine that POWs should be transferred from the collection centres to the POW shelter at Heliodrom, and the detainees who did not belong to that category should be sent to Gabela.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Perhaps you can help me out here. When I said that you decided or issued an order about the transfer of these individuals, and I'm referring to point 2, that persons who were not in the POW category should be transferred to Gabela and that the commission for the exchange from the office of the -- of displaced persons and refugees should be taken over, this isn't civilian power and authority. It is an order that from Heliodrom those should be transferred who do not belong to that category; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From Heliodrom persons were to be transferred who, on the basis of the categorisation, came under the competence of the office for exchanges in order to be exchanged. And we said that the transit centre was Gabela, when the order of the president of HR HB came for the disbanding of the centres, so that it exclusively refers to people being transferred from Heliodrom to Gabela.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Right. In point 1 of this order we see that in actual fact lists had already been compiled of prisoners or detainees who belonged to the prisoner of war category; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Or, rather, the word "prisoners of war" or "detainees" appears -- war detainees appears quite often, but prisoners of war would be a better term. Those who stayed in the POW shelter. So from all the other collection centres, the people who remained at Heliodrom were to be transferred to Heliodrom. That's the first point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I do not suppose having heard you for four days that you want to tell us that, and I quote, "people who remained at Heliodrom were to be transferred to Heliodrom"? That's lines 9 and 10 of page 69. You did not want to say that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. What I wanted to say was the following: The first point implies the fact that all detainees from other collection centres in -- that are in the category of detainees and remain within the POW shelter at Heliodrom should be transferred to Heliodrom. The second point is that those who were already at Heliodrom and did not belong to the category of detainees on the basis of the implementation of the decision were to go to Gabela, which was a transit centre. Is that clear or shall I explain it once again?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I just don't quite understand why persons who are to remain in Heliodrom should be transferred to Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I did not say that the people from Heliodrom were to be transferred to Heliodrom. We spoke about the implementation of the decision to close the collection centres, such as Gabela, Rama, Livno, Tomislavgrad, and of course Heliodrom. Now, those people who from the other collection centres were supposed to remain incarcerated were brought to Heliodrom, and this was regulated by point 1. Those who were at Heliodrom to begin with and needed to go to third countries or to the BH army side or to be released on the territory of HR HB were transferred to Gabela and competence and authority over them was taken by the commission for the exchanges and the office for displaced persons and refugees in cooperation with the ICRC.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. This is clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, just a follow-up question to be more precise. During your mandate, term of office, during the time you exercised your functions, were there detainees who had been condemned by military courts, convicted by military or civilian courts, and if so, where were they incarcerated? Where were they kept? If you know whether there were any convictions, and where were these people held?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think that I answered that question in a way earlier on. All those who stayed in the POW shelter at had Heliodrom, a criminal report was filed against them while I was in the area, but until then no legal proceedings were taken against them, and all of them were exchanged for those persons captured on the BH army side. And this was sometime at the end of April when this process was completed. Of course on the basis of the agreement of a truce and cease-fire and everything else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like to add a question to what my colleague just said. Your answer isn't very clear. My colleague wants to know whether the military courts, military Tribunals, condemned and convicted, whether there was a trial, whether there were legal proceedings and whether persons were convicted and condemned to a term in prison. In a word, did the military tribunals function? Did the military courts function, to the best of your knowledge? You arrived in November. Perhaps you don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The military courts started functioning. Now, if somebody was convicted they didn't come under the authority of the military police but under the Ministry of Justice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're not answering the question. My question was whether the military courts, tribunals, functioned, and, if so, as of what date? You weren't answering the question exactly. Perhaps you don't know, but that's my impression. You either know this or you don't know this. So there can't be any ambiguity and approximative answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, then I'd hear say that I don't know much about the work of the military courts and military prosecutor's office. The fact is that they had been established, and at the meeting when we discussed the disbanding of the collection centres, there were representatives of the military court of Mostar, Livno, the military prosecutor of Mostar, and the military prosecutor's office of Livno. They were all present. So I do believe that they were functioning, but they didn't come under my competence and authority, so I don't really have any information about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [No interpretation] [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours, I have the documents that would partly answer those questions of yours. I've been receiving English interpretation in my headphones. I have a document in my binder about the work of the military courts and military prosecutor's office, so we may be able to clarify this in a minute.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I've asked you about the selection that was carried out, and this was carried out by the commission which were established at the meeting to coordinate the whole thing, if we can call it that way.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, those were teams, four teams for four collection centres that existed at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Four teams for four collection centres. Very well. Do you know that even previously there were orders to the effect that there should -- a list of all the detainees should have been made, that they should be categorised? Did you ever come across such orders previously?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let's take a look at P 07148. The -- this is the record, and my colleague Ibrisimovic asked you about this document which was issued on the 11th December 1993. Have you found it? I'm referring to pages 5 and 6 in the B/C/S, and these are pages 11, 12, and 13 in the English version. Can we please look at the members of these teams and what their functions were. Can we conclude that the -- let's look at Gabela, Heliodrom, Livno, and Prozor. Would you agree with me that these were members of the SIS?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Of the military police?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The prosecutor's office?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The military tribunal?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And a member of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And in Heliodrom we have a doctor?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a doctor in Gabela as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: These were mostly representatives or members of the team whose task was to do what they were said to do, which was on page 6 in B/C/S and 13 in English; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It arises from these -- from the structure that there were no commanders as members of the team. The commander of Heliodrom was not a member of the team, although he had only been appointed by you as company commander.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We believed that they could not be members of these teams, that these should be people who had nothing whatsoever to do with the accommodation centres or shelters.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: At that moment.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Personal.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, personal. In that -- in other words, they were not employed at the shelters.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I meant. At the meeting on 13 December -- and this is the following document, P 07148. I'll refer you to page 4 in the B/C/S version and page 9 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you talking about the 13th? Are you referring to 748?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the counsel please repeat the number?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'm talking about page 4 in the Croatian version, and in the English version this is page 9, paragraph 6. The number is P 07143, just for the transcript. Did you find what Mr. Pogarcic has said? This is towards the end of the page. He says that criminal charges should be raised against individuals who are in the category of prisoners of war.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And the problem this -- that was being mentioned all the time; that was very topical. I would like to link it to the work of the judiciary and prosecutor's office -- offices at the time. I would kindly ask you to look at Exhibit P 06863. Did you find it?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is from the district military prosecutor's office in Mostar, 25 November 1993. They submitted information to the Ministry of Justice and the administration of Mostar about the number of criminal reports that they had received against members of the MOS, standing for the Muslim armed forces; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And follows a list of names, but there's no need for you to go into the list. The list contains 539 names; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I would like to state here that this letter is dated before the meeting when Mr. Pogarcic said that criminal reports should be filed against certain persons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. But criminal proceedings are not the same thing as criminal reports. I don't know whether Mr. Pogarcic knew the difference.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Pogarcic mentioned criminal reports.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that he meant criminal proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I apologise. We'll come back to that. Look at page 4.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Remind me of the number of the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The number of the document is P 07143. Again the meeting was held on the 13th. It won't be difficult for you to find it. On page 4, please.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I was reading the passage below. Could you go on and read it? The one above is okay. Mr. Pogacic believed that criminal reports should be filed, and I was reading the passage in which Mr. Pogacic said that there should be criminal proceedings carried out. I misunderstood you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: As my colleague Karnavas would say, can we take things at a time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In order to avoid ambiguities and for the benefit of the Judges, the document issued by the military prosecutor on the 25th of November refers -- I'm looking at Mr. Arif Pasalic. There is a list of 539 persons. Was he in prison or not? Was this document compiled based on complaints of the persons who were outside, who were not in there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can't answer your question because I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But Mr. Arif Pasalic, you knew him, didn't you? Did you know who Mr. Arif Pasalic was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I heard of Mr. Arif Pasalic, and I believe he was the commander of a BiH army corps, if I'm not mistaken. I the can't be sure of that, but name does ring a bell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well then. So this list mentions individuals who were not detained at the time, but there was investigation against them; is that correct.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will repeat that I don't know exactly. I can't answer your question. I don't know the answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I knew that you would raise this question, that you would notice that, but since we are in open session, I can't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Judges notice everything.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you look at the name under number 4? We are not going to mention the name in open session. This is a witness that was heard here and that on that day was in Heliodrom because he had been exchanged on the 29th of March, 1994. He was to be exchanged on that date. So this list also contains the name of the people who were at the Heliodrom at the time and remained there until they were finally exchanged, but it also contains the names of the people who were at large at the time. But that is topic that we will approach with other witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: What I'm saying, Mr. Witness, is that the military prosecutor's offices and judiciary worked at the time, that they filed criminal reports, and so on and so forth?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course the military worked. They filed reports. I believe that the court also worked, as was the prosecutor's office. This was not within my purview so I can't talk about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let's say something else about the -- about the court, although it is very -- probably difficult for the Trial Chamber to understand. Do you know how long would proceedings for such crimes last today? Would it have been possible for somebody to be convicted within two or three months at the time? Would it be possible today? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will only say that it would not be serious to pass any judgements within such a short period of time, but this is the only thing I can tell you because I don't have any experience in that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Do you agree with me since you were involved in such work as well that every criminal report that is filed implies certain operative work, checking information, and that it is only then that it is submitted to the prosecutor's office, that the prosecutor also performs checks, and it is only then that it is submitted to the court and -- and it is only then that the court will start proceedings against the individual in question?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the procedure that was in place.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It was in place then, and it is in place now?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Judge Trechsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I just recall that this witness is in no way an expert in the administration of justice or criminal justice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe you should move on to another topic, because the witness has told you that else not familiar with the practices of the judiciary. Don't waste your time on time. There is also the Judges' time, and the Judges can ask questions on anything, and this they do in your interest and in the interest of justice. In this particular area, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I -- my questions arose from your questions. Your Honours asked whether these people had been convicted. I just wanted to hear from the witness who participated in the course of his regular work in all the pre-trial phases of the proceedings, and I asked for his opinion. I did not expect him to provide his expert opinion, and this is not what I was after.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And finally, can we look at the next exhibit P 07269. This is your instruction or your guidance about the way prisoners of war should be treated. Can you tell me whether you have found it?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can we please look at number 1, taking prisoners. We can see the obligations that we have already mentioned, and these are the obligations on the part of the persons who were taking prisoners. And you state herein that -- this is under item 2, "Bringing in captives." It says that the duty officer in the shelter is duty-bound to take over prisoners of war from the persons who have brought them had in. And the remark here is that the person who -- can you please read it for us, because there is a typo here.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is a typo, so the word is who "brings them in." This is a typo.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So the persons who brings them in as to right a letter indicating all the personal data of the prisoners, place and time of the capturing, which actions were taken against them, and which actions are expected to be taken against these individuals. This is only logical. Do you believe that such instruction had existed even before in the HVO? Mr. Praljak has shown you a document, which I'll not be able to show you again, and this document says something to the same effect, that every soldier had to be aware of the fact that the captive had to be handed over to their subordinates who had to follow the procedure.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe there were such documents. General Praljak showed such documents yesterday and I explained why I repeated an act of the sort, why I reissued it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes. I was after that information. You knew that they existed. You just reached them. Now, that we have looked at all of the documents that originates from you, I would like to ask you three concluding questions that refer to this particular area. I have not asked you anything about the category of civilians. Judge Antonetti at one point asked you during the examination-in-chief about detained civilians, and you said in your answer, both on your chief as well as on cross-examination, that civilians could be removed from the areas of war operations into centres, and that in that case they were under the exclusive authority of the civilian authorities. And I'm referring to the Red Cross, the ministry for carrying -- about civilian prisoners. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is what I said. This is what I meant.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Based on the documents that we have seen about the disbanding of accommodation centres, we can see that the structures of the ministry of defence were involved, and I'm referring to the SIS and the military police, as well always the structures of the civilian authorities. And we saw that there were commissions of different nature. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: According to you, these structures, including military units that were involved in taking prisoners, had they had a previous obligation to treat prisoners of war and detainees in a certain way?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so, that -- because everybody who considers themselves a soldier should be aware of the basic rules of treating prisoners of war or civilians who were involved in war activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I need another three minutes for another exhibit that is very important, but I believe the time is to take our next break. Maybe you could tell me how much time I have spent so far and whether I will be able to finish for the next three minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you have the three minutes, and finish within these three minutes, and by doing that you will have finished your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Sir, this is very important to me. Yesterday you were shown a document, an exhibit, P 0787 [as interpreted]. Can you please look at it in your binder. P 07878. I'm sure you will remember this document.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you please turn to the following page -- we know more or less what the document is about. We have analysed it. But look at the first page, that's the page I'm interested in. On page 1 you see a list of individuals. This is the following page in the B/C/S version. I believe that the witness has located it. Under the list it says, "Kaznjenicka Siroki Brijeg, Siroki Brijeg, pursuant to the order of the coordinator from the president's office, Mr. Tomo Sakota, on the 1st of December, 1993."

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yesterday you were asked by the Prosecutor whether Mr. Tomo Sakota had been appointed as a coordinator?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I didn't know what his role as a coordinator was.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can we please look at the following exhibit, which is P 07341.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes, that's the number. Could you please look at the last page to see who the signatory of the document is? And this is actually the second page of the document.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Tomo Sakota.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Right. Tomo Sakota. And can you give me the date?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 26th of December.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: 1993; right? So there's no doubt that it's the same person. And we can take a look at the first sentence on first page just to confirm what it said previously.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says that the coordinator for inmates and prisoners of war on the territory of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, that he was appointed.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And what does it say?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As coordinator for inmates and prisoners of war on the territory of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna. I was appointed by President Mate Boban.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can we agree that it's the same person?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I assume there weren't two people with the same first and last names.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And that completes my cross-examination, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, and what I'm going say concerns Mr. Karnavas and Counsel Nozica, you speak of Tomo Sakota. In the document presented by Mr. Karnavas, at page 157 -- 2757 it says, Tomo Sakota who was an object of somebody who was being looked for. Is that the same person? But we're going to take a 20-minute break and reconvene at five minutes past 6.00. This is a person that's being pursued. Now, if there's time left over I'll give the floor to Counsel Alaburic and Mr. Praljak, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hearing is resumed. Before I give the floor to Mr. Mundis, an oral decision concerning a Defence request with respect to the admission of exhibits. Mr. Kovacic has asked to exceed the number of words. So the Chamber has considered the matter and allows Mr. Kovacic to exceed the number of words. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, with all due respect, I'm wondering about the procedural road that we're going down with respect to redirect examination, perhaps to be followed by reopening of cross-examination. I'm -- to be quite frank, the general practice has been in most trials here that the party calling the witness is given the final opportunity for redirect examination and the motion of reopening or reopening cross-examination should be based upon -- if it were to be based upon the re-examination then it's, of course, impossible for the Defence to know what issues I'm re-directing on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're quite right. I understood it that Mr. Praljak and Counsel Alaburic didn't want to broach new subjects. That's not permitted, as you said, but to be more specific on certain points. So in the interests of the Defence, the Chamber is going to grant them that opportunity. You can have your redirect. They can have their 10 minutes. And if by chance, although that would be -- if they overstepped that ruling, then I would give you the floor again. If they did broach a new topic. So rest assured that your rights are guaranteed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I may, and I'm speaking on behalf of my client, and I'm sure other Defence feel the same way, under this procedure, one counsel could get up and implicate, say, somebody else, or might have an effect on another accused, and therefore now others might want to ask questions as well. So I'm not saying I disagree with the Court's ruling, but, you know, others may wish to then re-clarify the clarifying point that hadn't been clarified in the initial cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak, what did you wish to clarify? What point?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to clarify what the law governing the armed forces was, who enacts what decisions, what the armed forces are in war, what the supreme commander is, what the relationship is between the chief of the Main Staff to engage forces, but if you don't think that is necessary, then I won't do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that we could consider those matters with other witnesses. There will be other witnesses to address those issues, but we have understood your concerns, and we'll deal with that with other witnesses. Counsel Alaburic. There'll be other witnesses that you can ask those questions of.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we keep waiting for an expert witness, an expert witness on the army to clarify certain concepts.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence of Mr. Coric yesterday broached numerous subjects with respect to the work of the military police, and I consider that they are exceptionally important in these proceedings, and my colleague, Ms. Tomasegovic, did not have enough time, as she said herself, to look through all the documents and round off the topics she had. Now, since we have a witness here who is extremely well-versed in military police matters, and I'll tell you the subjects exactly, the combat engagement of military police units, because it remained unclear who was authorised to decide on engaging the military police in combat. We can resolve that question in two minutes. Also, the military police battalions in the operative zones and whether they are subordinated to the commanders of the operative zones. And the third important subject is the brigade military police which was not within the establishment of the regular military police. That's not contested, but it would be important to establish the tasks and assignments of the military police. Now, in 10 minutes' time we can deal with those matters on the basis of a few documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He has already answered those three questions. I personally could give you answers to those three questions myself, but you seem to feel that the witness has not answered them. I'll give you the 10 minutes. What did you want to add, Ms. Tomic?

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like to say that since there's going to be direct reference to my client and questions that deal with his responsibility and accountability in this trial, I think it would be highly unjust that, after Ms. Alaburic, I was not given additional time to deal with the problems that Mr. Karnavas raised before me, and I completely agree with what he said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The questions that she's going to ask are questions that were already broached, and we had a document on them. So, Counsel Alaburic, you have 10 minutes, not a minute more, to ask your three questions, but as far as I'm concerned I think the witness has already answered them. Perhaps you didn't realise this.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have prepared a set of documents, and if they haven't been distributed amongst Your Honours, please may they be distributed, and I have a set for the witness too.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have to react. These are not just three questions. These are documents that we're going to it show now, new documents we're going to be looking at, and I really object. I think I have every right to cross-examine on these documents after my colleague Ms. Alaburic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no -- nothing against Ms. Tomic asking additional questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Use your 10 minutes, and then we'll see whether we're going to allow Ms. Tomic to reply. You took us by surprise. I didn't think you were going to raise some new documents. During the break we spoke with the registrar about a document -- about files with 1.000 exhibits, and now we have hundreds and hundreds of documents to deal with every day. So one should be superhuman to get through all this. And now, to top everything, you present us with another 150 pages of documents that we're going to have to assimilate in the space of 10 minutes' time. Now, we're not superhuman, so I'd like to let you know that, but go ahead with your 10 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I completely agree that if you so desire I -- I won't be tendering these documents into evidence, but they could just serve as a basis for my questions, because we'll get through this much faster than we would without these documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Biskic, yesterday General Praljak and Mr. Coric asked you questions about the light assault battalions both in the Republic of Croatia and in HR HB. So I'd like to ask you the following: Were they military police battalions which were established to take part in combat activities?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Madam, Counsel, let me repeat the answer I gave you yesterday. I said that in the Republic of Croatia there was a Light Assault Battalion of the military police intended to perform combat operations. As far as the light assault battalions of the military police, I don't know why they -- what they were specifically intended for, because in the military police of the Croatian army we had anti-terrorist units. They were intervention forces to deal with the most complex military and police assignments.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's move on and we'll see on the basis of the documents. Can we agree, to begin with, that up until the 1st of September, 1993, on the territory of the Herceg-Bosna, one Light Assault Battalion existed which covered the whole of the Herceg-Bosna territory, and after that, subsequently, four light assault battalions were established for each operative zone, one for each operative zone? Do we agree on that score?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said when I spoke about the establishment up to my arrival that there existed four battalions in the military districts or for South-east, Western and Eastern Bosnia, and Posavina, and that there were four light assault battalions in each of those zones. That's how I understood the establishment.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right. Now take a look at document P 00978, please, and it is -- they are rules and the systematisation of tasks in the administration of the MP, military police, and I'd like to look at point 1 which relates to the chief of the military police. What were his tasks or authorisations? He was in charge of managing and organising the work of the military police administration. He performed functions of cooperation with the organs and services of the HZ HB. He commanded military police units, and in brackets it says battalions in the operative zone and the Light Assault Brigade. Now, my question is based on this break-up of posts, does it not emerge that the chiefs of the military police had authority to command both battalions in the operative areas or military districts and the Light Assault Battalion -- Light Assault Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's move on to the next document which you've already seen. It is P 00957. And the document is from the head of the defence department and chief of the military police administration dated December 1992 on the establishment of the military police. And look at page 1, please, line 7, and it says the 1st Battalion of the military police is directly linked to the military police administration and it is active in that respect, and pursuant to an order by the chief it can be active all over the territory of the HZ HB. From this document, does it emerge that the Light Assault Battalion is commanded by the chief of the administration of the military police? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I didn't understand it that it talks about Light Assault Battalions. This is an active battalion. I suppose it was attached to the department for defence and that's why it was engaged all over the territory of HR HB.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Would you read out the third sentence? It says the 1st Company, et cetera, et cetera, specially trained and so on and so on. So that's what we're dealing here. That the company within the frameworks of this active battalion was precisely this Light Assault Battalion that we are talking about; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't confirm that answer because I understand this differently. Perhaps I'm wrong, but as far as I'm concerned the Light Assault Battalions of the military police were established later, not on the 26th of December.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
