utterances.text: Sir, it says for this active battalion it is composed of the command, the communications, and three companies. The 1st Company is the light assault unit specially trained for emergency interventions or anti-terrorist activity. So from this, can we conclude that we are dealing with a unit which is capacitated to act as an Anti-Terrorist Unit just like the light assault brigades or, rather, the units of the military police in the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that in Croatia we had a special anti-terrorist military police and the Light Assault Brigade was different. Now, in the armed forces it was just for combat operations and came under the chief of the Main Staff fully, under his command completely, and the anti-terrorist units were within the composition of the military police and it was the battalion commander who was in charge.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers kindly speak more slowly. It is impossible to translate at this rate. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation] [Interpretation] Because I have so little time, I apologise. I'm trying to squeeze everything into the little time.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Mr. Biskic, just for the record, I have referred you to the regulations on the work of the administration of the military police, but we cannot compare. We don't have the time.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can explain, if the Trial Chamber wishes me to do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Maybe at the end if I have another minute left, because I want to go through the following questions. Tell me, please -- go to page 3, please. On page 3, the third paragraph from the bottom, does it say that the MP administration commands all units of the military police?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you now look at document 4D 00509. I don't know whether we have it in the e-court. This is a scheme of the military police which was taken from a report of the military police for this first half of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're talking about the regulation?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: No. I'm talking about the scheme. And the document number is 4D 00509. This is a scheme, and just for an additional explanation I will tell you what document the scheme has been taken from. I'm showing the document. It is in the electronic court. Mr. Biskic, according to your information, is this the way the military police was organised from 1st of July, 1993?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the organisation that I found when I went down there, but this organisation is not the same as it was on the 26th of December.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Absolutely not. This would be reorganised military police. But the document that we spoke about a while ago from 1992 is one type of organisation, and the new document speaks about the organisation that was in place in 1993. According to what you know, Mr. Biskic, the assistant chiefs of the MP administration, were they given the authorities of the chiefs of the MP administration, and were they in the control of the light assault company as well as the companies within their territory?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is how I understood these documents when they were shown to me by the Defence of Mr. Valentin Coric.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's look at document P 03000. This is a letter by the chief of the MP administration, Mr. Coric, dated 28 June 1993, in which he wrote to all the commanders of the military police companies about the new reorganisation that was to be put in place on the 1st of July 1993. Can we look at the 3rd Company -- third paragraph from the bottom it says the merger of all the military police activities by military assault company and military police company in the operative zone will be carried out by the assistant commander for that zone who will be in command of the companies. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: We were talking about the combat operations of the MP units, and you told us that in December 1993 the military police no longer was engaged in any combat operations. Could you please tell us whether the reason for that was the fact that light assault companies were separated from the military police, they were disbanded, and members of these light assault companies were -- became members of the HVO? Was that the reason?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose that this was one of the reasons. So the answer is yes. But even before the light assault -- light assault companies were disbanded, I asked the chief of the Main Staff to issue an order, and this was issued but it was implemented only towards the end of December, but the fact is that light assault companies were the foundation of the organisation of guards brigades.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I would just like to draw your attention to the fact that in the document you have already seen several times over the past several days about the meeting of the officers of the military police, which took place on the -- 14 December. On page 6 of the Croatian text, Mr. Lavric's words were recorded to the effect that light assault units were disbanded and would from then on be under the authority of the Main Staff of the HVO. Could you please look at document P 03778. This is an order by the chief of the MP administration, dated 28 July 1993. And by this order it is ordered to several military units, which I'm not going to go through, everybody can read them -- those for themselves, these units of the military police will be resubordinated to the commander of the HVO or the commander of the respective operative zone that the commander authorises. Does it arise from this paragraph that the chief of the military police was authorised to resubordinate the units of the military police to an HVO commander?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This arises from this order.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the following paragraph. It says here, the assistant chiefs are authorised to issue an order based on their best judgement to involve other companies or platoons of the military police within their operative zones in the aforementioned companies. Does it arise from this that further combat engagement of the military police was something that an officer of the military police was authorised to decide on? Can we please look at the third paragraph? It says here: "Assistant chiefs -- assistant chief are duty-bound to --" Mr. Biskic, could you please repeat the answer to the question whether the additional engagement of the units of the military police in combat operations was something that an officer of the military police was authorised to decide?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Assistant chiefs were authorised to act on this decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My colleagues are saying that you have exhausted your time, Ms. Alaburic. Mr. Coric, is there something that doesn't make -- doesn't tally in the witness's answers? You're an expert. We have already seen the documents. There's nothing new. Is there something that calls for a clarification on the part of the witness? If that is the case, go ahead he and put your questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to point to the document that is on the screen. I would like to show the document that preceded this document. It will take me only two minutes. It is in my binder. Maybe the document that my colleague has just shown be put on e-court. This is P 03778. Can we please have it on e-court again. The colleague asked for it a minute ago. And can we please look at the heading where it says: "In keeping with the order of the head of the defence department, number 02/1/914-93, dated 28 July 1993." Let's keep this in our memory. And then I would call for another document in e-court, and the Judges have in it in my binder. Unfortunately I did not have time to show these documents yesterday. I was going to but I didn't have the time. This is document P 02002 -- 5D 02002. 5D 02002, can we have this on e-court. While we're waiting for the document to be placed on the e-court, this is an order that Mr. Coric is referring to dated 28 July 1993. The order is on the operative resubordination of the military police and to avoid reading the entire document, I'm going to read just 1, 2, and 3. "All units of the military police which are to be added to the force, of the HVO until the task is completed shall be resubordinated to the commander of the HVO. "The military police in that case shall carry out tasks that will be given to it by the commander of the HVO. "I hereby request that all units of the military police should be provided with this order as soon as possible in order to avoid any future misunderstandings between the commander of the HVO and the commander of the HV -- military police." In this regard I have two very short and very simple questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Go ahead and ask your questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, yesterday I showed you a report for the period from January to June. I told you also there would be reorganisation and this would be carried out in order to be more operative in the times of war. Was it customary or is it customary in every armed force in the world, when they're faced with a war, that in an a single operative zone all units are resubordinated to the strongest unit by formation, and that for the troops to function and for the troops to carry out their combat tasks and all the other tasks on the ground that this resubordination means a merger of all units and that in this case the assistant chief of the operative zone, regardless of the formal link-up with the military police in the performance of his tasks, it would be the chief of the operative zone who would be his superior. That's my question.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If you look at these two orders, then this is what arises from these two orders.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you will allow me, Your Honour. If you will allow me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment. Mr. -- we are not going into any further discussions. Mr. Coric, do you have in -- a question that would arise from the witness's answers and that have to do with your position, the position that you held at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CORIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Given my questions yesterday, which were more detailed and more specific about combat activities, would you adhere to yours answers to those questions?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would adhere to my answers that I gave yesterday, and to the answers that I provided about the specific documents.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CORIC
utterances.text: I'm going to repeat that question that was put to you by my lawyer. In any operative zone, when there are combat operations going on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are -- you are repeating the same question. Is --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CORIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have not finished my question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Go ahead then, but we were under the impression that you repeating the same question which was not the meaning.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CORIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CORIC
utterances.text: Could the military police be in charge of the cooperative operations in an operative zone without the commander of that operative zone?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED CORIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Nozica, you wanted a clarification on a document. This could last forever. One document and another document, a document arising from a document.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not going to take for ages. Two documents where Bruno Stojic have been shown and I'm now in a situation to seek clarification, but what I'm trying to tell to the Trial Chamber is that there's no need for us to do this through this witness. We will have experts on the side of the Prosecution and on the side of the Defence who will be better suited to clarify all of this. This is what I'm -- I'm saying, because some documents that originated from my client have been shown.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you allow me just two words because I would like to provide some explanations to my colleagues. If we had had some more time, then my colleagues would have shown documents that would have not caused this misunderstanding, and we are not disputing the authorities of an HVO commander of the units of the military police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, your additional questions. You're additional questions have to be directly linked to the questions that were put in the course of the cross-examination, but I'm sure you know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Biskic.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I have just a few questions, and they mainly stem from two precise or two discrete topics. One of them, sir, relates to some questions put to you by Ms. Alaburic yesterday concerning the relationship, if you will, between a newly formed army and that army's compliance with the law, and let me start by asking you this, sir: It's certainly the case that in the time period that you were in Bosnia-Herzegovina the HVO was still in the process of being formed. Is that your opinion? Is that your view?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the HVO, I would say, was at war all the time, in the process of formation o being re-established or established.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, the relationship between an army in the process of being established under wartime conditions and the obligations of commanders in such -- faced with such a situation to ensure compliance with international law obligations?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At all levels of command starting out from a squad commander and then further up, everybody at his level must take the measure -- the kind of measures that you've just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, my question, sir, was a little bit more precise. When an army is in the process of being established under wartime conditions, what impact, if any, does that have upon these obligations of military commanders to ensure compliance with the law?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I've understood the question correctly, then my answer would be the following: Of course it is more difficult to wage a war, at the same time, to maintain security over the army, security in the area where combat operations are taking place, and further afield as well, if I understand your question correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, the answer, sir, seems to go to maintaining security over the army and security in the area, but my question really goes to the obligation of the commander to ensure compliance with international law obligations. Do those obligations continue notwithstanding the fact that the army in question is in the process of being established under wartime conditions?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said yes, but of course it was difficult to ensure that all that was applied. But of course that is what one must do regardless of the prevailing conditions and conditions under which one has to function.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'd next like to turn, perhaps with the assistance of the registrar, to P 04756, which was a document which was shown to you yesterday. Perhaps we can have that in e-court, P 04756. Mr. Biskic, do you remember looking at this document yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can we please go in the B/C/S version or Croatian version to page 3, and the English version to page 4. And I'm specifically, sir, asking you to take -- or to turn your attention to item 3. Do you see that in the document, sir?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see the beginning of item 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Perhaps if it's --

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see page 3. I can see item 4 and part of the text of item 3 but not the whole of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If we can go in the Croatian version to page 2. I believe it starts at the bottom of page 2. And then if we could then go to --

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see the beginning of that sentence now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If we could then go to the following page in the Croatian version, please. Now, yesterday, I believe it was, the Defence for Mr. Coric asked you to read out part of this document. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And if memory serves me, sir, you were asked specifically to read out the last part under item 3 immediately above where Mr. Lucic -- or the comments of Mr. Lucic are recorded. Do you see that part that begins with

utterances.speaker: MR. CORIC APPARENTLY SAYING
utterances.text: "My opinion is that we have two military prisons"?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Heliodrom and the military prison at Ljubuski. As for other places -- this is a little illegible. I had a better document in front of me yesterday. "As for other places where," and then I can't read that. And then in brackets, "(Gabela and Dretelj), I consider that they are not military ones and I don't stand behind the work in those institutions."

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Biskic, can you continue reading the comments of Mr. Lucic.

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Lucic says: "I consider that we cannot pass over the problems of the prison in Gabela and Dretelj just like that and that that can do us a lot of harm. We must say quite explicitly who is behind those prisons, who is doing that, and what we can do to take certain steps."

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Biskic, with respect to these comments that were purportedly made by Mr. Lucic where he says, "We must say precisely who is behind prisons," by the time of your arrival in Bosnia and Herzegovina in November 1993, was that question or those questions answered to your satisfaction? In other words, did you know who was behind Gabela and Dretelj?

utterances.speaker: MARIJAN BISKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I think I've already answered that question. I said from the letter by the deputy head of the military police administration, dated the 17th of November, 1993, it was stated that the security should be provided by the Home Guard Units, and a precise answer as to who was in charge, who was responsible for that, I never received that answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Biskic, thank you again for coming to The Hague and answering everyone's questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, I would like to thank you for having come. You have spent hours answering questions put to you. You have gone through hundreds and thousands of pages. So I would like to express our gratitude and our best wishes for a safe return back to your own country and every success in your new activities in the private sector. I would like to ask the usher to escort you out of the room.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, too, and good-bye.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd just like to correct the transcript on page 98, lines 7 and 8, what I said wasn't fully recorded. I said that I -- we do not challenge the responsibilities and authorisations of the HVO commander over those units of the military police which were resubordinated to that commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We have that in the transcript now. I would like to say two things before we close for the day. I would like to thank and congratulate Mr. Karnavas for the fact that he went through one topic after another and enabled us to follow, and it would be a good idea if the other Defence counsel were inspired by the technique applied by Mr. Karnavas, which would facilitate us in the cross-examination. I would also like to congratulate Ms. Nozica, who provided binders with two colours. One colour for non-admitted documents and another colour for admitted documents, which has facilitated our work. So that was a good contribution, and we'd like to express our thanks there. Now, as regards next week's witness, we have decided to grant the Prosecution three hours, and the Defence will have 30 minutes for each team, with the exception of Mr. Petkovic, who will be accorded one hour, and it's up to you, of course, to distribute the time amongst yourselves as you see fit. It is almost 7.00. We adjourn until Monday at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 12th day of March, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.
